The student effectively details their responsibilities and key projects, such as leading sound healing sessions, conducting workshops, designing communications, and creating the Solidarity room.
citations: I had the privilege of being a Jean Donovan Fellow through Santa Clara University, partnering with Urban Sanctuary and Recovery Cafe San Jose.
I worked 30-35 hours a week as a Spirituality and Social Justice Intern.

I led trauma-informed sound healing sessions, conducted workshops on the subconscious mind and compassion, served meals, designed weekly digital communications for the chapel, participated in healing circles, and listened and learned deeply from the stories of members.

One of my favorite projects this summer was creating the Solidarity room in Urban Sanctuary, where I collaborated with a local artist on its design. Then I created descriptions for different art pieces commemorating individuals who have fought in solidarity with social justice causes.

detailed_results.feedback: The student articulates a rich and diverse set of learnings, encompassing personal growth (empathy, self-acceptance), societal insights (systemic failures, ostracization), organizational understanding (non-profit inner workings), and practical skills (holding sacred space, leadership, communication). The reflections are deep and demonstrate significant personal and professional development.
citations: This summer has opened my heart to empathy, love, and healing in a whole new way.

I gained a deeper understanding of myself and the marginalized communities in San Jose. I learned about how many systems in society, from housing, healthcare, and food, fail to create rehabilitative services for those coming out of incarceration, homelessness, or mental health disorders.
I also learned about the inner workings of a non-profit organization as I sat with the finance committee at the Sanctuary while they reviewed their annual budget.
I learned how to hold sacred space and lead this summer. I led sound healing for the community members and guided meditations. I led a workshop on the subconscious mind and inner child healing.
It made me realize the importance of the words I choose and the need to be clear/intentional about them.

detailed_results.feedback: The essay clearly identifies a specific 'difficulty' or surprise related to the use of the word 'Icon' in a survey. citations: One difficulty that I encountered this summer was with my work in Urban Sanctuary.
A woman in the church came up to me and was upset that I used the word Icon. She said that she didn’t want us to be worshipping the individuals in the room.

I felt compelled to send this community member an email to clarify her questions and address her feedback. I explained the definition of "Icon" to her, contrasting it with the one she had in mind. I clarified and responded to her questions. She responded with gratitude.

detailed_results.feedback: The essay provides a detailed and insightful analysis of the organization's operations through the EMPAC framework. The student clearly identifies and explains elements related to Matching (database system), Price (behavioral rules vs. free monetary cost), Access (services, location), and Cycle (re-enrollment process, daily schedule), demonstrating a strong understanding and application of the model.
citations: For matching, the Cafe uses a system to input all the new members' information. This database is utilized across the various Recovery Cafes to share information in case a member needs to switch locations or otherwise.

The “price” for entry or becoming a member at the cafe requires following the three main rules: being clean and sober for 24 hours, completing two chores a month, and attending your weekly recovery circle.
Members gain access to meals, recovery support services, classes, and workshops.
If the members do not abide by these rules, they will have to restart at orientation and could eventually have to wait a couple of months for re-enrollment if these rules are not met.
Therefore, the EMPAC model of this organization is designed to engage members who are actively involved in and moving toward recovery and healing.
